definition: The training objective in which a language model learns to predict the most likely next token given the preceding sequence of tokens.
details: This deceptively simple objective, applied at massive scale, is the core mechanism by which LLMs learn grammar, facts, reasoning patterns, and style from raw text.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. That blueprint is Next-Token Prediction.
